title: Choosing a tool noun
summary: Pick the operation by the kind of evidence you need, then follow its typed descriptor into the lifecycle.
audience: A research-agent author or contributor deciding which Attune capability should perform a step.

sections.heading: Repository establishes and advances the subject

claims.text: Use repository materialization to establish an exact base and repository checkpoint to turn an intentional workspace change into the next snapshot. These are lifecycle operations, not general Git wrappers.

Use Joern when the question is about code-property-graph structure. The operation accepts either the typed query projection or an explicit raw query with a result schema at the lower library boundary.
Use Maude to retain a formal module and command result as native evidence. Its request is scoped to the investigation rather than treated as a free-standing shell command.
Use the property runner when an executable invariant should be tested and minimized. Seed, path, run counts, and counterexample data remain part of the typed result.
Use ast-grep when a structural rule should be scanned or rewritten. Writer policy remains explicit, so a rewrite is distinguishable from a read-only scan in both the type and lifecycle layers.
